```{r packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(DBI)
library(RSQLite)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 11))
tidymodels_prefer()
```

# Goal

We predict whether a scheduled departure from BOS will leave **15 or more
minutes late**, using only information that is available before departure:
the schedule (hour, day of week), the carrier and destination, the distance,
the proximity to a federal holiday, and the weather observed at BOS just
before the scheduled departure hour.

# Data

```{r load}
con <- dbConnect(SQLite(), "data/bos_flights.sqlite")

model_data <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT flight_date, crs_dep_hour, day_of_week, carrier, dest, distance,
         temp_c, dew_point_c, rel_humidity, visibility_km, wind_speed_ms,
         wind_gust_ms, precip_mm, rain, snow, fog_mist, thunder, any_precip,
         dep_del15
  FROM flights_weather
  WHERE cancelled = 0 AND diverted = 0 AND temp_c IS NOT NULL
")

dbDisconnect(con)
```

```{r features}
# U.S. federal holidays in the study period
holidays <- as.Date(c("2025-09-01", "2025-10-13", "2025-11-11",
                      "2025-11-27", "2025-12-25", "2026-01-01",
                      "2026-01-19", "2026-02-16", "2026-05-25",
                      "2026-06-19", "2026-07-04"))

model_data <- model_data %>%
  mutate(
    flight_date = as.Date(flight_date),
    delayed = factor(if_else(dep_del15 == 1, "delayed", "on_time"),
                     levels = c("delayed", "on_time")),
    day_of_week = factor(day_of_week, levels = 1:7,
                         labels = c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri",
                                    "Sat", "Sun")),
    days_to_holiday = map_dbl(flight_date,
                              \(d) min(abs(as.numeric(d - holidays)))),
    days_to_holiday = pmin(days_to_holiday, 7)
  ) %>%
  select(-dep_del15)

nrow(model_data)
```

## Time-based split

To mimic real use (predicting future flights), we train on the earlier
months and test on the last three months instead of splitting at random.

```{r split}
train <- filter(model_data, flight_date < as.Date("2026-06-01"))
test <- filter(model_data, flight_date >= as.Date("2026-06-01"))

split <- make_splits(train, test)

tibble(set = c("Training (Sep 2025 - May 2026)", "Test (Jun - Aug 2026)"),
       flights = c(nrow(train), nrow(test)),
       delay_rate = c(mean(train$delayed == "delayed"),
                      mean(test$delayed == "delayed"))) %>%
  knitr::kable(format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, digits = 3,
               format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
               caption = "Training and test sets")

# Flights on the same day share the same weather and the same daily
# disruptions, so a random split would put very similar flights in both the
# analysis and assessment sets. We therefore keep each day together in one
# fold (grouped cross-validation by date).
set.seed(5110)
folds <- group_vfold_cv(train, group = flight_date, v = 5)
```

## Preprocessing recipe

```{r recipe}
rec <- recipe(delayed ~ crs_dep_hour + day_of_week + carrier + dest +
                distance + days_to_holiday + temp_c + dew_point_c +
                rel_humidity + visibility_km + wind_speed_ms + wind_gust_ms +
                precip_mm + rain + snow + fog_mist + thunder + any_precip,
              data = train) %>%
  step_novel(carrier, dest) %>%                      # levels unseen in training
  step_other(carrier, dest, threshold = 0.005) %>%   # pool rare categories
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) %>%
  step_zv(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())
```

# Models

We compare four models: a majority-class baseline, L1-regularized (lasso)
logistic regression, a random forest and gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost).
Hyperparameters are tuned with 5-fold cross-validation on the training set,
grouped by date, using ROC-AUC as the selection metric.

```{r specs}
base_spec <- null_model() %>%
  set_engine("parsnip") %>%
  set_mode("classification")

lasso_spec <- logistic_reg(penalty = tune(), mixture = 1) %>%
  set_engine("glmnet")

rf_spec <- rand_forest(trees = 300, mtry = tune(), min_n = tune()) %>%
  set_engine("ranger", importance = "impurity",
             num.threads = parallel::detectCores()) %>%
  set_mode("classification")

xgb_spec <- boost_tree(trees = 500, tree_depth = tune(),
                       learn_rate = tune()) %>%
  set_engine("xgboost", nthread = parallel::detectCores()) %>%
  set_mode("classification")

metrics <- metric_set(roc_auc, pr_auc)
```

```{r tune, cache = TRUE, dependson = c("split", "recipe", "specs")}
set.seed(5110)
lasso_res <- tune_grid(workflow(rec, lasso_spec), resamples = folds,
                       grid = grid_regular(penalty(c(-5, -1)), levels = 10),
                       metrics = metrics)

set.seed(5110)
rf_res <- tune_grid(workflow(rec, rf_spec), resamples = folds,
                    grid = grid_regular(mtry(c(3, 15)), min_n(c(10, 40)),
                                        levels = 2),
                    metrics = metrics)

set.seed(5110)
xgb_res <- tune_grid(workflow(rec, xgb_spec), resamples = folds,
                     grid = grid_regular(tree_depth(c(3, 6)),
                                         learn_rate(c(-2, -1)),
                                         levels = c(2, 3)),
                     metrics = metrics)
```

```{r cv-results}
bind_rows(
  show_best(lasso_res, metric = "roc_auc", n = 1) %>% mutate(model = "Lasso"),
  show_best(rf_res, metric = "roc_auc", n = 1) %>%
    mutate(model = "Random forest"),
  show_best(xgb_res, metric = "roc_auc", n = 1) %>% mutate(model = "XGBoost")
) %>%
  select(model, mean, std_err) %>%
  knitr::kable(format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, digits = 4,
               col.names = c("Model", "CV ROC-AUC", "Std. error"),
               caption = "Best cross-validated ROC-AUC on the training set")
```

# Evaluation on the test set (Jun - Aug 2026)

Each tuned model is refit on the full training set and evaluated once on the
test months.

```{r final, cache = TRUE, dependson = c("split", "recipe", "specs", "tune")}
final_fit <- function(res, spec) {
  workflow(rec, spec) %>%
    finalize_workflow(select_best(res, metric = "roc_auc")) %>%
    last_fit(split, metrics = metrics)
}

fits <- list(
  "Baseline" = last_fit(workflow(rec, base_spec), split, metrics = metrics),
  "Lasso" = final_fit(lasso_res, lasso_spec),
  "Random forest" = final_fit(rf_res, rf_spec),
  "XGBoost" = final_fit(xgb_res, xgb_spec)
)

test_preds <- imap_dfr(fits, \(f, name) collect_predictions(f) %>%
                         mutate(model = name))
```

```{r test-metrics}
test_preds %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  summarise(roc_auc = roc_auc_vec(delayed, .pred_delayed),
            pr_auc = pr_auc_vec(delayed, .pred_delayed)) %>%
  # a constant (no-skill) prediction has a PR-AUC equal to the share of
  # delayed flights; yardstick's value for a constant score is not meaningful
  mutate(pr_auc = if_else(model == "Baseline",
                          mean(test$delayed == "delayed"), pr_auc)) %>%
  arrange(desc(roc_auc)) %>%
  knitr::kable(format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, digits = 3,
               col.names = c("Model", "ROC-AUC", "PR-AUC"),
               caption = "Test-set performance (Jun - Aug 2026)")
```

```{r roc, fig.height = 4.6}
test_preds %>%
  filter(model != "Baseline") %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  roc_curve(delayed, .pred_delayed) %>%
  ggplot(aes(1 - specificity, sensitivity, colour = model)) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_path(linewidth = 0.9) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(title = "ROC curves on the test set (Jun - Aug 2026)",
       subtitle = "Dashed line = random guessing (baseline)",
       x = "False positive rate", y = "True positive rate (recall)",
       colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## Precision and recall at a decision threshold

Because only about a quarter of departures are delayed, the default 0.5
threshold flags very few flights. We therefore also report results at a
threshold of 0.30, close to the delay rate in the training data.

```{r thresholds}
threshold_metrics <- function(preds, thr) {
  preds %>%
    mutate(pred = factor(if_else(.pred_delayed >= thr, "delayed", "on_time"),
                         levels = c("delayed", "on_time"))) %>%
    summarise(threshold = thr,
              accuracy = accuracy_vec(delayed, pred),
              precision = precision_vec(delayed, pred),
              recall = recall_vec(delayed, pred),
              f1 = f_meas_vec(delayed, pred))
}

test_preds %>%
  filter(model != "Baseline") %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  group_modify(\(df, key) bind_rows(threshold_metrics(df, 0.5),
                                    threshold_metrics(df, 0.3))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  knitr::kable(format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, digits = 3,
               col.names = c("Model", "Threshold", "Accuracy", "Precision",
                             "Recall", "F1"),
               caption = "Classification metrics at two thresholds (test set)")
```

```{r confusion}
best_model <- test_preds %>%
  filter(model != "Baseline") %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  summarise(auc = roc_auc_vec(delayed, .pred_delayed)) %>%
  slice_max(auc) %>%
  pull(model)

best_model

test_preds %>%
  filter(model == best_model) %>%
  mutate(pred = factor(if_else(.pred_delayed >= 0.3, "delayed", "on_time"),
                       levels = c("delayed", "on_time"))) %>%
  conf_mat(delayed, pred)
```

## Feature importance

```{r importance, fig.height = 4.6}
# gain-based importance from the fitted XGBoost model
xgb_booster <- extract_fit_engine(fits[["XGBoost"]])

xgboost::xgb.importance(model = xgb_booster) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  slice_max(Gain, n = 15) %>%
  ggplot(aes(Gain, fct_reorder(Feature, Gain))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2c7fb8", width = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Top 15 features (XGBoost, gain-based importance)",
       x = "Share of total gain", y = NULL)
```

```{r save-results}
# save the results used by the final report (report/report.Rmd)
saveRDS(list(
  cv = bind_rows(
    show_best(lasso_res, metric = "roc_auc", n = 1) %>% mutate(model = "Lasso"),
    show_best(rf_res, metric = "roc_auc", n = 1) %>%
      mutate(model = "Random forest"),
    show_best(xgb_res, metric = "roc_auc", n = 1) %>% mutate(model = "XGBoost")
  ),
  test_preds = test_preds,
  importance = as_tibble(xgboost::xgb.importance(model = xgb_booster)),
  test_delay_rate = mean(test$delayed == "delayed")
), "data/model_results.rds")
```

# Interpretation

**Cross-validation vs test performance.** With cross-validation grouped by
date, the cross-validated ROC-AUC on the training months (0.723 for the
lasso, 0.740 for the random forest and 0.742 for XGBoost) is close to the
ROC-AUC on the test months (0.743, 0.733 and 0.745). An earlier version that
used ordinary random folds gave much higher cross-validated values for the
tree models (about 0.78) that did not hold up on the test set. Because flights
on the same day share the same weather and disruptions, random folds let the
tree models partly memorize individual days. Grouping by date gives honest
estimates and is the approach we use.

**Model comparison.** All three models perform far better than the
majority-class baseline (ROC-AUC 0.5). XGBoost has the highest test ROC-AUC
(0.745) and PR-AUC (0.543, about twice the no-skill value of 0.266), but the
differences between the models are small: the lasso logistic regression is
only 0.002 lower in ROC-AUC. A simple, interpretable linear model therefore
captures most of the predictable signal, and the tree models add little.

**Decision threshold.** At the default threshold of 0.5 the models flag few
flights as delayed (recall of 10.5% for the lasso and 30.0% for XGBoost),
because delays are the minority class. At a threshold of 0.3, XGBoost
identifies 53.4% of the delayed flights (recall), and 50.7% of the flights it
flags are actually delayed (precision). In the test months, this means 5,318
of the 9,968 delayed departures are flagged, along with 5,172 on-time
departures. Accuracy is a poor guide here: XGBoost's accuracy of 73.8% is
barely above the 73.4% that would be obtained by always predicting "on time".

**Important features.** The scheduled departure hour is by far the most
important feature, accounting for roughly 40% of XGBoost's total gain. This
agrees with the exploratory analysis, where the delay rate rose from under
10% in the early morning to over 40% in the evening as delays propagate
through the day. Weather variables follow (relative humidity, temperature,
dew point and visibility), together with distance, proximity to a holiday and
the carriers with the highest delay rates (Southwest, JetBlue and Spirit).

**Limitations.** First, the models cannot use month, because the summer test
months do not appear in the training data, and the test period had a higher
delay rate (26.6%) than the training period (23.3%). Second, late-arriving
aircraft cause almost half of all delay minutes, but the models have no
information on whether the inbound aircraft is late; adding the delay of each
aircraft's previous flight (via its tail number) is likely the largest
possible improvement. Third, the weather is measured only at BOS, so weather
at the destination or elsewhere in the national system is not captured.
Finally, the analysis covers a single airport and a single year.
